claims.text: Deficiency in short-chain fatty acid (SCFA) production is associated with type 2 diabetes mellitus.
A select group of SCFA-producing bacterial strains is promoted by dietary fibers in patients with type 2 diabetes.
Most non-promoted potential SCFA producers are either diminished or unchanged in patients with type 2 diabetes receiving dietary fiber intervention.
Greater diversity and abundance of fiber-promoted SCFA producers lead to improved hemoglobin A1c levels in patients with type 2 diabetes.
Fiber-promoted SCFA producers improve hemoglobin A1c levels partly via increased glucagon-like peptide-1 production.
Promotion of fiber-responsive SCFA-producing bacteria diminishes bacterial producers of metabolically detrimental compounds such as indole and hydrogen sulfide.

methodologies.name: Randomized clinical study with high-fiber dietary intervention and fecal shotgun metagenomics
methodologies.description: A randomized clinical study evaluating specifically designed isoenergetic diets combined with fecal shotgun metagenomic profiling in patients with T2DM.
conditions: Specifically designed isoenergetic dietary fiber intervention
